# Ezekiel 17 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** The LORD spoke to me again:

**2** "Son of man, give the people of Israel a riddle — tell them a story.

**3** Say to them: The Lord GOD says: A great eagle with enormous wings, long feathers, and beautiful plumage swooped down to Lebanon and snapped off the top of a cedar tree.

**4** He carried the treetop away to a land of merchants and planted it in a city of traders.

**5** Then he took a seed from the land and planted it in fertile soil beside a plentiful water supply, setting it out like a willow tree.

**6** It sprouted and became a low, spreading vine. Its branches turned toward the eagle, and its roots grew down beneath it. It became a vine, producing branches and sending out shoots.

**7** But then another great eagle appeared — also with huge wings and thick plumage. And this vine twisted its roots toward the second eagle and stretched its branches toward him, wanting him to water it instead of the garden where it had been planted.

**8** Yet it had been planted in good soil with plenty of water — everything it needed to produce branches, bear fruit, and become a magnificent vine."

**9** Ask them: The Lord GOD says: Will this vine thrive? Won't the first eagle tear it up by the roots and strip off its fruit until it withers? All its green leaves will dry up.

**10** Ask them: The Lord GOD says: Will this vine thrive? Won't the first eagle tear it up by the roots and strip off its fruit until it withers? All its green leaves will dry up.

**11** Ask them: The Lord GOD says: Will this vine thrive? Won't the first eagle tear it up by the roots and strip off its fruit until it withers? All its green leaves will dry up.

**12** Ask them: The Lord GOD says: Will this vine thrive? Won't the first eagle tear it up by the roots and strip off its fruit until it withers? All its green leaves will dry up.

**13** Ask them: The Lord GOD says: Will this vine thrive? Won't the first eagle tear it up by the roots and strip off its fruit until it withers? All its green leaves will dry up.

**14** Ask them: The Lord GOD says: Will this vine thrive? Won't the first eagle tear it up by the roots and strip off its fruit until it withers? All its green leaves will dry up.

**15** Ask them: The Lord GOD says: Will this vine thrive? Won't the first eagle tear it up by the roots and strip off its fruit until it withers? All its green leaves will dry up.

**16** As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, the king of Judah will die in Babylon — in the land of the king who put him on the throne, whose oath he broke and whose treaty he violated.

**17** Pharaoh and his mighty army won't be able to help him when Babylon builds siege ramps and walls to destroy countless lives.

**18** He broke his oath. He violated the treaty. He shook hands on the deal and then broke every promise. He will not escape.

**19** The Lord GOD says: As surely as I live, he broke My oath and violated My covenant. I will bring the consequences down on his own head.

**20** The Lord GOD says: As surely as I live, he broke My oath and violated My covenant. I will bring the consequences down on his own head.

**21** The Lord GOD says: As surely as I live, he broke My oath and violated My covenant. I will bring the consequences down on his own head.

**22** The Lord GOD says: "But I Myself will take a shoot from the very top of the tall cedar and plant it. I will snap off a tender twig from the highest branch and plant it on a tall, prominent mountain.

**23** I will plant it on the high mountain of Israel. It will grow branches, bear fruit, and become a magnificent cedar. Birds of every kind will nest in it and find shelter in the shade of its branches.

**24** And all the trees in the field will know that I am the LORD. I cut down the tall tree and make the short tree grow tall. I dry up the green tree and make the dead tree flourish. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **17:3-6**: The riddle of the two eagles is a political allegory in disguise. Eagle one is Babylon's king. The cedar-top is Judah's deported king. The vine is Zedekiah, the puppet king left behind.

- **17:7**: Zedekiah reaches out to Egypt for help — breaking the oath he swore to Babylon. It's not just bad politics; he swore that oath in God's name. Breaking it is breaking faith with God.

- **17:22-24**: After all this political disaster, God says: 'I'll do the planting Myself.' He'll take a tiny twig and grow it into a magnificent tree. When humans wreck everything, God starts over — from something impossibly small.

— PNEUMA
